title: The Heavens, O Lord! Thy Power Proclaim
description: The Heavens, O Lord! Thy Power Proclaim in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 178 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night showeth knowledge."”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: The heavens, O Lord! thy power pro-claim, And the earth ech-oes back thy name; Ten thou-sand voi-ces speak thy might, And day to day, and night to night, Ut-ter thy praise thou Lord a-bove! Thy praise, thy glo-ry, and thy love.

lines: The heavens, O Lord! thy power proclaim,
And the earth echoes back thy name;
Ten thousand voices speak thy might,
And day to day, and night to night,
Utter thy praise — thou Lord above!
Thy praise, thy glory, and thy love.
And nature with its countless throng,
And sun, and moon, and planets' song,
And every flower that light receives,
And every dew that tips the leaves,
And every murmur of the sea —
Tunes its sweet voice to worship Thee.
Thy name thy glories they rehearse,
Sense of all sense, and soul of soul,
Nought is too vast for thy control;
The meanest and the mightiest share
Alike thy kindness and thy care.

licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
